facts.text: Kashiwara sits about 20 kilometres from Osaka’s centre, overlooking the Yamato River that once linked the ancient Yamato Basin to the sea.
The city’s name, Kashiwara, echoes its ancient roots, with archaeological finds dating back to the Paleolithic era proving continuous settlement for thousands of years.
During the Kofun period, Kashiwara became a burial mound hub, thanks to its strategic position along the Yamato River.
In the Edo era, Kashiwara was a tenryō territory directly governed by the Tokugawa shogunate, reflecting its importance in regional control.
The city once thrived as a dye‑making centre, especially for yukata robes, though most of that industry has faded under overseas competition.
Kashiwara’s eastern edge rises into the Ikoma Mountains, where Mount Kongō borders Nara Prefecture, giving the town a varied landscape from flat plains to rugged hills.
